backlog.spec: For the first starts, use a perturbed grid-like initial layout instead of a uniform random one: rows of 5,5,6,5,5 (or 6,5,5,5,5) circles with jitter of sd 0.02, plus radii initialised to 0.05. Also try hexagonal-like row patterns chosen at random by seed. The best known packings for n=26 are near these ring or row structures.
backlog.title: Structured initial layouts

backlog.spec: Add a kick type, chosen with probability 0.3. Remove the 2 or 3 circles with the smallest radii. Place them at random points that are at least 0.05 from the walls, and set their radii to 0. Then run the usual two-phase solve with the other circles' radii kept. Accept by the existing rule.
backlog.title: Single-circle relocation of smallest circles

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, restrict the pairwise non-overlap constraints to pairs whose centres are within a cutoff of the start configuration, for example distance < 2 * (max radius in start) + 0.25. Build the pair index list once per call from the start centres and use it in cons and cons_eq. Keep a full-pair final check in _repair so validity is still guaranteed. Fewer constraints means a much smaller SLSQP problem per iteration, so more iterations fit into the time budget.
backlog.title: Sparse neighbour-pair constraints

backlog.spec: Keep a separate current state (c_cur, r_cur) in addition to the global best. Each kick starts from the current state. After repair, the new state replaces the current state if its radius sum is at least the current sum minus a tolerance eps = 2e-4. The global best is updated whenever a new sum beats it, as before. This lets the walk drift across near-equal packings instead of always returning to the single best. Use eps as a module-level constant.
backlog.title: Plateau random-walk acceptance

backlog.spec: In the slot-35 disc kick, replace the uniform re-randomisation inside the disc with a per-circle perturbation. Compute each circle's slack as its radius minus the smallest radius in the best packing, or use the count of near-contacts. Add Gaussian noise to every centre with sd = 0.05 * (1 + rank-based small-circle weight), and zero the radii only for circles in the disc. Keep the rest of the loop unchanged.
backlog.title: Slack-proportional per-circle kicks

backlog.spec: Before the kick's free-radius SLSQP, scale all radii of the best packing by 0.9. Keep the disc re-randomisation as is. This gives all the circles slack, so the optimiser can rearrange more easily. The phase-1 equal-radius solve is skipped for kicks, and SLSQP starts directly from the shrunk state.
backlog.title: Radius-shrink then regrow kick

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, when start is None, skip phase 1 (the tied-radius optimisation). Instead build the start from random centres in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW] and radii drawn from rng.uniform(0.03, 0.13, n), then go straight to phase 2. Phase 1 pushes every start toward equal-size packings, which are far from optimal mixed-size ones. Starting with mixed radii gives more diverse and often better basins. Leave the kick path unchanged.
backlog.title: Random varied initial radii, skip equal-radius phase

backlog.spec: Change the acceptance rule in solve so that a new candidate replaces the current working solution whenever its radius sum is at least (best sum - tau), where tau starts at 0.01 and decays linearly to 0 over the time budget. Track the global best separately and return it at the end. The current working solution is what gets kicked; the global best is what gets returned. This lets the search drift across neighbouring basins early and focus later.
backlog.title: Threshold acceptance of slightly worse packings

backlog.spec: With probability 0.25 in the kick branch, use a global move instead of the disc kick: c = best centres + rng.normal(0, 0.015, (n, 2)), clipped to [0, 1], and r = 0.85 * best radii. Then re-optimise with _solve_once from this start, repair, and accept if better. The disc kick changes local structure, while this move nudges the whole contact network at once and can slide rows of circles together, which a local disc cannot do. Keep the other 75% of kicks as they are.
backlog.title: Global small-jitter kick mixed with disc kicks

backlog.spec: In the SLSQP constraints, include only pairs whose centre distance in the starting point is less than 0.5, recomputed at each kick (the pair set is fixed within one minimize call). After the solve, verify all pairs, and let the repair or LP fix any violations. This cuts the constraint count from 325 to about 100 and speeds up each iteration substantially.
backlog.title: Only active pair constraints

backlog.spec: After optimisation, fix the centres and solve a linear program using scipy.optimize.linprog (HiGHS) to maximise the sum of radii subject to r_i+r_j<=d_ij, r_i<=wall distance, r>=0, with d_ij reduced by 1e-12. Use the result in place of the heuristic shrink repair, then subtract SHRINK. This recovers the loss from the repair step and gives an exactly feasible packing.
backlog.title: Tighter repair using exact LP radii

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform re-randomisation in the disc kick with a directional displacement. Pick a random angle theta and a stretch factor s uniform in [2, 4]. For each circle inside the disc, add to its centre a Gaussian displacement with standard deviation 0.08 along the direction theta, scaled by s, and 0.08 perpendicular to it. Clip to the square, set the radii of the displaced circles to 0, and re-optimise with _solve_once. The displacement is elongated along one direction, which moves circles through the gaps of their neighbours more easily than an isotropic shake.
backlog.title: Anisotropic Gaussian displacement kick

backlog.spec: Add a second move type, used with probability 0.3 instead of the disc kick. Take the current best, find the circle with the smallest radius, and remove it. Sample 3000 uniform points, compute each point's clearance min(wall distances, min_j(|x - c_j| - r_j)), and put the removed circle at the point with the largest clearance, with radius 0. Then run _solve_once with this start, clip, repair, and accept if it beats best. Small circles that rattle in poor holes get moved to the biggest gap.
backlog.title: Rattler relocation move

backlog.spec: In solve, replace the uniform random kick centre p with the point of largest empty space. Draw 200 uniform candidate points in [0,1]^2, compute each candidate's distance to its nearest circle centre (or to the walls, whichever is smaller), and set p to the candidate with the largest such distance. Keep the disc radius R and the disc re-randomisation unchanged. The kick then targets the holes of the incumbent, where rearrangement is most likely to pay off.
backlog.title: Kick centred on the largest empty region

backlog.spec: Add a second kick type to solve, used with probability 0.4 (the disc kick otherwise). Pick a random circle i, then a random circle j whose radius differs from r_i by more than 0.02. Swap their centres (c[i], c[j] = c[j].copy(), c[i].copy()). Keep the radii attached to their indices, then scale both radii down to min(r_i, r_j) so the start is near-feasible. Re-optimise with _solve_once from that start vector. Topological swaps reach neighbouring basins that a local disc perturbation rarely finds.
backlog.title: Swap kick: exchange two circles of different size

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, when a start is given (the kick path), build the pair list only from pairs (i, j) with |c_i - c_j| - r_i - r_j < 0.3 at the start point, and use these pairs in place of the full triu_indices in cons. Keep all wall constraints and r >= 0. This shrinks the constraint Jacobian from 325 rows to roughly 100-150, so each SLSQP iteration is much cheaper and more kicks fit in the budget. Overlaps between pairs left out are caught by _repair, which still checks all pairs. Fresh restarts keep using all pairs.
backlog.title: Sparse neighbour pair constraints in phase 2

backlog.spec: With probability 0.5, apply two independent disc kicks in the same iteration instead of one. Draw two disc centres p1 and p2 and two radii R1 and R2 from the existing ranges, re-randomise the circles inside each disc, and set their radii to 0. The union of the two regions is then re-optimised with a single _solve_once call from the combined start. Keep the acceptance rule and all other settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Two-disc compound kick

backlog.spec: After computing the candidate (c, r), instead of relying on _repair to shrink radii, run one extra SLSQP phase on the radii only with centres fixed at the clipped values. Use the constraints: r_i >= 0, r_i <= distance to each wall, and r_i + r_j <= d_ij for all pairs. Maximise the sum of r. Only then apply _repair as a safety net with the tolerance kept at zero shrink, so that the repaired sum is not discarded. The aim is to recover the radius mass that the crude shrink step throws away.
backlog.title: Replace shrink-repair with a final re-optimisation of radii

backlog.spec: Add a fast pre-optimiser before the SLSQP phases. Minimise minus the sum of radii plus a quadratic overlap penalty mu * sum(max(0, r_i + r_j - d_ij)^2) plus a wall penalty of the same form, using scipy L-BFGS-B with bounds on all variables. Run it for mu in [1e2, 1e3, 1e4, 1e5] in sequence, warm-starting each step. Pass the output to the existing SLSQP phase 2 as the start. Cheap penalty steps should land in good basins that SLSQP then polishes.
backlog.title: Penalty continuation with L-BFGS before SLSQP

backlog.spec: Instead of always kicking from the best, keep a current solution and accept the new candidate if its sum is greater than current - T, with T about 0.003 decaying linearly to 0 over the time budget. Keep best separately and return it. This helps escape local optima while still exploiting.
backlog.title: Basin-hopping acceptance with current state

backlog.spec: In the kick loop, make the disc radius R decay linearly over the time budget. R goes from 0.35 at the start to 0.12 at the end, instead of being uniform in [0.15, 0.35]. Keep a random factor in [0.7, 1.3] around the scheduled value. Everything else stays as in slot 35.
backlog.title: Kick radius schedule

backlog.spec: Keep a 'current' solution separate from 'best' in solve. Each kick starts from current rather than best. Accept a new solution as current if its sum is larger, or else with probability exp((new_sum - cur_sum)/T). T starts at 0.004 and decays linearly to 0 by the end of the time budget, computed from elapsed process time. Update best whenever new_sum > best_sum. Also, if current has not improved best for 40 consecutive kicks, reset current to best. This lets the search leave a basin it would otherwise never escape.
backlog.title: Annealed acceptance of kicked solutions

backlog.spec: Change TIME_FRACTION from 0.8 to 0.92 (CPU time limit is 30 s, hard void at 45 s). Make sure a single SLSQP call is unlikely to overrun by checking the average iteration time and stopping the loop if the elapsed time plus the last iteration's duration exceeds 0.95*time_limit.
backlog.title: Raise TIME_FRACTION to 0.92

backlog.spec: Change the acceptance rule of the kick walk. Keep a current state separate from the best state. Accept a candidate if its sum is at least current - T, with T decaying geometrically from 0.004 to 0.0002 over the time budget. Kick from the current state and return the best state seen. Do not add chains.
backlog.title: Accept-equal-or-slightly-worse walk

backlog.spec: In solve, in the local-kick branch, change the disc radius draw from R = rng.uniform(0.15, 0.35) to R = rng.uniform(0.08, 0.25). Smaller discs move fewer circles (about 1-5) per kick, so each kick is cheaper for SLSQP to repair and more of them are accepted. Change nothing else.
backlog.title: Smaller kick disc radius

backlog.spec: In both cons and cons_eq, replace the pair constraint sqrt(dx^2+dy^2) - r_i - r_j >= 0 with dx^2 + dy^2 - (r_i + r_j)^2 >= 0 (and 4t^2 in the equal-radius phase). The feasible set is the same for nonnegative radii, but the constraint is smooth everywhere: it has no sqrt singularity when centres coincide, which matters after kicks that drop centres close together. SLSQP's finite-difference Jacobian is then better conditioned. Change nothing else.
backlog.title: Squared-distance pair constraints

backlog.spec: Keep an elite list of the top 5 distinct packings by radius sum (discard duplicates whose sum is within 1e-6 of an existing entry). On each kick, choose the parent uniformly at random from the elite list instead of always using the single best. Insert a new result into the pool if it beats the worst entry. Return the best entry. This diversifies the search without changing the local optimiser.
backlog.title: Elite pool with random parent selection

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, run a short L-BFGS-B minimisation on the energy -sum(r) + mu * sum(max(0, overlap)^2) over the walls and pairs, with mu increasing over 3 stages (10, 100, 1000), starting from the random initial layout and with radii initialised to 0.07. Pass the result to SLSQP phase 2 directly, skipping phase 1. This gives a better-conditioned start.
backlog.title: Penalty-based pre-relaxation

backlog.spec: Change the kick to be cheaper and more varied. Choose among three moves at random: re-randomise circles in a disc of radius 0.1-0.25, remove the smallest circle and reinsert it at the largest-hole location (a random point with the maximum distance to other circles, from 2000 samples), or swap the positions of two circles with different radii. Set the radii of the moved circles to 0 before re-optimising.
backlog.title: Smaller, more local kicks

backlog.spec: Add a compaction kick as an alternative move with probability 0.3. Scale every centre of the incumbent toward (0.5, 0.5) by a factor f drawn uniform in [0.95, 0.99], so that slack appears along the walls. Set all radii to 0.9 times their incumbent values, then re-optimise with _solve_once from this start. The move reorganises the whole packing and is cheap to code, since it needs only one vector operation before the existing local solve.
backlog.title: Compaction kick

memo: Helped: changes to how each solve searches. Slot 8 (equal-radius SLSQP before the free solve) gave -2.6311/-2.6311. Slot 35 (local disc re-randomisation kick) is the incumbent at -2.6343/-2.6354 (delta -0.0037, 2 runs, mean -2.6349). Local-search walks beat fresh restarts: slot 11 gave -2.6354/-2.6334 and slot 27 gave -2.6341/-2.6324. Replica exchange (-2.6348) and the two-island model (-2.6349) tie the incumbent, so more chain machinery adds nothing. No effect (+0.0000): TIME_FRACTION 0.93, LP repair, warm restarts, successive halving. Hurt: radius-weighted restarts (+0.0165), log-barrier (+0.0045), L-BFGS-B penalty (+0.0034), MAX_ITER 1000 (+0.0019). Start-diversity tweaks are exhausted. Next: tune the kick size, disc radius and acceptance rule of slot 35, and polish the best packing at the end. Replicate any gain, since noise sd is 0.0023. Keep the code simple.
